- When sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- Model consistently overpredicts early in the 30-day horizon, especially after price spikes; apply downward bias of 2–5% for days 1–5.
- After a sharp price increase, model often overshoots in the following 3–5 days; cap forecast at 1–2% below true peak.
- If sentiment is neutral or negative (≤0.1), model underestimates downward trends; add 1–3% to forecast to account for mean reversion.
- Model fails to capture mean reversion in the 10–15 day window; adjust forecast to align with 7–10 day moving average of true prices.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to underestimate the final 5–7 days; add 1–3% to last 5–7 forecast values to match true outcome.
